title: Emrys and the Witness
premise: Noor Underhill, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, catalogues a confession letter that arrives postmarked the day after the funeral of Canon Elias Wren — a letter claiming Wren was murdered and naming Noor's late mother as witness. As Noor investigates, he discovers his mother's hidden past entwined with the cathedral's locked crypt and an inheritance that was never meant to reach him. The killer is Detective Inspector Sable Voss, who once worked the original case file and has been quietly erasing every trace of what the tide took from the crypt forty years ago. In the climax, Noor lures Voss into the crypt at low tide with forged evidence; Voss confesses to protect her father's name, and Noor must choose between turning her in and honoring the love they've grown into — he chooses duty, but keeps one letter back as inheritance for the truth.
about_author: M. M. Okonkwo is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade among ledgers, seals, and locked drawers before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who find the dead in paperwork.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A week after Canon Wren's funeral, a confession letter arrives dated after his death, claiming murder and naming Noor's mother. Noor files it properly, then reads it again by lamplight. The beat: grief interrupted by dread — the first crack in his orderly world.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. He petitions the chapter to open the sealed crypt and is refused by Dean Halloway, who seems more frightened than protective. Noor finds his mother's name scratched inside an old visitor ledger. Beat: curiosity hardening into resolve; the archive becomes a crime scene.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, introduced as sympathetic. DI Sable Voss reopens Wren's death unofficially, haunted by a forty-year-old drowning case she once closed too fast. She notices someone else pulling the same file. Beat: professional unease — two hunters circling the same paper trail.

chapters.title: Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Among his mother's effects he finds letters proving she witnessed something in the crypt decades ago and was paid to forget. Her 'accidental' death reframes itself. Beat: betrayal and tenderness tangled — the parent he mourned becomes a stranger.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Another letter arrives, this time at the police station, contradicting the first — someone is staging confessions. Voss realizes the killer knows the case file intimately: dates, evidence numbers, even her own marginalia. Beat: the hunter realizes she's being hunted through her own records.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At low tide, exposed mud beneath the sea wall yields a rusted strongbox — his mother's, holding the original crypt key and a photograph of three young people: Wren, the dean, and a woman whose face is torn out. Beat: awe curdling into fear as the past surfaces literally.

chapters.title: Choir of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Noor and Voss meet, each concealing what they know, trading half-truths over tea. Their wary alliance sparks something warmer. Meanwhile Halloway lies about his whereabouts on the night Wren died. Beat: intimacy built on mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Torn Photograph
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss identifies the torn face: her own father, the officer who closed the original case. She confronts the archive of her family's complicity and realizes the killer is protecting him — or avenging him. Beat: identity shattered; duty and blood pull opposite ways.

chapters.title: Ebb
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, climax. Noor plants forged evidence naming the torn woman and waits in the crypt at low tide. Voss comes — she is the author of both confessions, killing Wren to bury her father's crime forever. Trapped by rising water, she confesses; Noor chooses arrest over mercy. Beat: heartbreak at the moment of triumph.

chapters.title: Accession
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the crypt opens lawfully; the bones of the original victim are named and buried. Noor catalogs everything except one letter — Voss's last, addressed to him — which he seals into the archive under his mother's name. Beat: quiet inheritance; love preserved as record rather than lived.
